newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan grounds relief plane it says helping rebels.
newsitem.headline: Sudan grounds relief plane it says helping rebels.

text.p: Sudan said on Sunday it had grounded a relief plane it said was masquerading as a supply aircraft for the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA).
Army spokesman Mohammed el-Senoussi told state radio Omdurman that officials grounded the plane after it landed without a permit at the airport in Bor town in the southern Jonglei state.
There was no independent confirmation of the report.
Senoussi did not give any details about the identity of the plane and the passengers or when the incident took place but said that all the people on board the plane were detained.

He said that the state had evidence the plane was serving the rebel SPLA which has been fighting for autonomy of the mostly Christian and animist south from the Islamist Arabised north for the past 13 years.

"The plane was working under the guise of relief and humanitarian work to serve the aims of the outlaws and regional plots seeking to undermine the country and its national sovereignty," Senoussi said.
"The pilot was interrogated whereby some important documents he was intending to hand over to other circles were found," he added.

Rebels led by the SPLA launched an offensive against goverment troops in January and Sudan says they are merely working on the orders of hostile neighbours Uganda, Ethiopia and Eritrea. All three states deny any involvement in the fighting.
Late last year, pro-government southern militias grounded a relief plane, ferrying three Red Cross workers, which landed in their territory by mistake.
The workers -- an Australian, a Kenyan and an American -- were released five weeks later after a U.S. congressman intervened.
